1,0,1: Luke Badiali reviewed five recent proposals with Chris and Leanne. Discovery is thin, qualification is informal and proposals are long and methodology heavy. We agreed a structured discovery call with the operating partner and a shorter proposal format.
5,1,1: Define pipeline stages and exit criteria to match the new process.
5,2,1: Leanne to export all open opportunities with stage and value.
2,1,1: Two of the five losses came after 30-page proposals that never mentioned the investment case. Chris accepted the proposals were written for plant managers, not operating partners.
2,2,1: Discovery calls are usually with the plant manager. Leanne said they rarely ask about the hold period or the exit plan.
2,3,1: There is no shared definition of a qualified opportunity, so partners spend time on proposals that were never likely to close.
3,2,1: Every discovery includes the operating partner and covers 6 set questions, including hold period, EBITDA target and exit timing.
3,7,1: Cap proposals at 8 pages, opening with the EBITDA bridge from the investment case.
3,3,1: Adopt a simple scoring of budget owner, value-creation plan link and start date; do not write a proposal below 2 out of 3.
3,8,1: Run a monthly pitch review where Leanne coaches partners on two live opportunities.
4,2,0: Rewrite the proposal template to the 8-page format
